h1: The 5 Best Small Safes for Money of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Small Safes for Money: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five small cash safes from Bonsaii, Voncabay, Yuanshikj and others, compared by access method, mounting and budget.
summary: The Bonsaii 0.23 cu ft is the best small safe for money because its USB-C emergency power means a dead battery will not lock you out. The Voncabay adds a three-try lockout, and the two-code steel box suits shared cash. Choose the 0.6 cu ft Bonsaii for more space, or the Yuanshikj for the lowest price.
intro: Most buyers shop a cash safe by steel gauge and forget the one failure that actually locks people out: a keypad battery that dies on the day you need the money. A box that cannot open is just a heavy paperweight, and replacing a battery is no help when the batteries sit inside the sealed door. The practical question is how each safe behaves when power fails and how hard it is to carry away.

We ranked five small safes from their listings, scoring access methods, mounting, capacity and price bucket on the Primea framework. None of them claims a fire or burglary rating, so treat all five as everyday cash and valuables storage, not protection against a determined thief or a house fire.

products.name: Bonsaii Small Safe Box with Electronic Keypad for Valuables, 0.23 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: USB-C emergency power means a dead battery will not lock you out.
products.description:
The Bonsaii 0.23 cu ft is a mountable steel box with an electronic keypad, pre-drilled installation holes and a USB-C port for emergency power. That port is the detail that matters. Keypad safes fail at the worst moment when batteries run flat, and a USB-C backup lets you power the lock from a phone charger and open it instead of cutting the door.

It leads because that fallback removes the biggest practical risk of owning a keypad safe. The Voncabay beside it adds a lockout feature but no power port, and the Yuanshikj behind it has no USB-C either. All three share a similar $25 to $50 class on price.

Buy it for household cash you must be able to reach in any situation. The interior is only 0.23 cu ft, roughly a shoebox, so measure your largest envelope first. No fire rating is listed.
products.idealFor: Households that cannot risk a dead-battery lockout.
products.skipIf: You need more than a shoebox of space.

products.name: Voncabay Money Safe Box for Home with Digital Keypad, 0.23 Cu. Ft., Black
products.verdict: Three wrong codes trigger a five-minute lockout.
products.description:
The Voncabay is built around deterrence. A 0.23 cu ft mountable steel box with a digital keypad, it locks out for five minutes after three wrong entries. That delay turns code guessing from a minute-long job into an hours-long one, which matters when kids, guests or cleaners share the room.

It takes second because it relies on the keypad alone. Without the Bonsaii's USB-C port, a flat battery has no listed rescue, so the lockout feature has to earn its place against that risk. The bundled document bag is described as fireproof and waterproof, but that is a bag, not the safe, and should not be treated as a rated container.

Buy it if code guessing is your worry and you will replace batteries on schedule. Skip it if a dead battery is the scenario that scares you more, since no emergency power is listed.
products.skipIf: You want an emergency power port.

products.name: Digital Electronic Money Safe, Steel Security Lock Box with Keypad, Office
products.verdict: Two independent access codes for shared cash.
products.description:
The unbranded 4.6 liter box is the shared-access pick. SPCC steel construction, a mountable design and a carpet liner come in a $25 to $50 package, and the key feature is two independent access codes. That lets two people open the same safe with their own codes, so a household or small office does not need to swap a single shared number.

It ranks third because the two-code feature helps only shared users, and the Bonsaii models offer a broader safety net in USB-C backup. The price is similar to the Voncabay, but the generic branding means you have less to go on if something fails.

Buy it for a small office or a two-person home. The caveat is the missing backup: no emergency power or override key is listed, so check for that option before you buy and keep spare batteries on hand.

products.name: Bonsaii Safe Box with Electronic Keypad for Home Office, 0.6 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: The roomiest safe here, with two 18mm bolts and a removable shelf.
products.description:
The larger Bonsaii is the roomy option, with 0.6 cu ft of interior and a removable shelf for sorting cash from papers. Two 18mm steel locking bolts hold the door, and it offers three ways in: code, key or USB-C emergency power. Bolt diameter matters because thicker bolts resist prying better than thin pins.

It ranks fourth for price and size, not quality. At $50 to $100 it costs a bucket more than the small safes, yet it gives more than double their space, and it matches the smaller Bonsaii on backup. Its access options are the best in the ranking, so a lower placement here reflects bulk and budget only.

Buy it for larger cash volumes, documents or small valuables. For a few bills, it is overkill, and it needs more wall or shelf space to mount.
products.skipIf: You only store a little cash.

products.name: Yuanshikj Small Steel Security Safe Box with Keypad, Key, 0.23 CuFt, Black
products.verdict: The cheapest anchored safe, with dual steel bolts.
products.description:
The Yuanshikj is the cheapest anchored safe here. It is a 0.2 cu ft mountable steel box with dual steel locking bolts, a magnetic auto-lock door and mounting hardware included, all in the under $25 bucket. Magnetic auto-lock means the door latches when you close it, so you cannot forget to secure it.

It sits last only because the Bonsaii models add USB-C backup and the Voncabay adds lockout, and this one has neither. Capacity is the smallest listed, so it suits a handful of bills and a passport more than stacks of cash. Dual bolts still give it real holding power for the price.

Buy it for a first, low-cost box. Anchor it with the supplied hardware, because an unbolted small safe can simply be carried away. Keep a spare key outside the safe, since no emergency power is listed.
products.idealFor: First-time buyers on a tight budget.

whatMatters.detail: A keypad safe runs on batteries, so a USB-C port or a backup key is what stops a dead cell from locking you out. The Bonsaii models list USB-C emergency power, and the 0.6 cu ft one adds a key. Look for emergency power or override key in the listing, and keep spare batteries in a drawer.

A bolted-down safe is much harder to carry off, and small safes are the easiest to steal because a thief can walk out with the whole box. Mounting turns a lightweight container into a fixed one. Check that pre-drilled holes are listed and that screws or bolts are included, as with the Yuanshikj, and plan to use the supplied hardware.

Locking bolts are the steel pins that hold the door shut, and thicker ones resist prying much better than thin latches. The larger Bonsaii lists two 18mm bolts, the Yuanshikj lists dual steel bolts. Look for bolt diameter and count in the specs, and be wary of listings that only say heavy duty without a figure.

A wrong-entry lockout slows code guessing by freezing the keypad after a few bad attempts. The Voncabay locks for five minutes after three wrong entries, which turns a quick guess into an hours-long job. It matters when kids, guests or staff share the room. Look for the number of tries and the delay in the bullets.

Capacity is interior volume, and small safes fill faster than the spec suggests once you stack envelopes, passports and a drive. The 0.23 cu ft models hold a shoebox worth, the 0.6 cu ft Bonsaii more than double that. Compare interior dimensions, not exterior size, and measure your largest item before ordering, including a laptop or document folder.

faq.a: No. None of these list a fire rating. The Voncabay bundles a document bag described as fireproof and waterproof, but that is a bag, not the safe itself, so do not rely on the steel box to survive a house fire.
Leaving the safe unmounted. A small box can be carried away whole. Use the pre-drilled holes on the Bonsaii or the hardware included with the Yuanshikj to anchor it to a stud or concrete.

faq.q: Is the larger Bonsaii worth it?
faq.a: Only if you need the room. The 0.6 cu ft Bonsaii adds a shelf, two 18mm bolts and a key option, but for a few bills and a passport the 0.23 cu ft version is enough and costs less.

Several include pre-drilled holes and hardware, so use them to anchor the box to a wall stud or floor. The Yuanshikj ships with bolts, and the Bonsaii models list installation holes, so you may only need a drill.

Keypads need batteries, and they die. The Bonsaii models offer USB-C emergency power so you can still open the door, while the Voncabay and two-code box list no backup, so replace cells before they weaken.

faq.q: Can I keep the key inside?
faq.a: No. Keep spare keys outside the safe, in a different room if possible. A key locked in with the cash defeats the purpose, and the larger Bonsaii's key option is only useful if the key is accessible.

finalTake: For most buyers, the Bonsaii 0.23 cu ft is the best small safe for money because USB-C emergency power keeps a dead battery from becoming a lockout. Pick the Voncabay if code guessing worries you, the two-code box for shared cash, and the 0.6 cu ft Bonsaii if space matters. None of them carries a fire rating, so store only what you can afford to replace.
